nodes.label: Interruptibility Principle
nodes.rationale: Apple's WWDC guidance holds that every animation must be interruptible and redirectable at any moment because the user's thought and gesture happen in parallel; locking input during a transition breaks the illusion of direct manipulation.

nodes.label: Apple's Eight Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Purpose, Agency, Responsibility, Familiarity, Flexibility, Simplicity, Craft, and Delight are framed as serving four human needs (safety/predictability, understanding, achievement, joy); Delight is explicitly the result of getting the other seven right, not decoration added on top.

nodes.label: Animation Decision Framework
nodes.rationale: Four ordered questions (should it animate, what is the purpose, what easing, how fast) gate every animation decision so motion is justified rather than decorative.

nodes.label: Scale(0) Anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the real world disappears/reappears completely from nothing, so entrances should start from scale(0.9+) with opacity, not scale(0), to look natural.

nodes.label: Sonner Principles
nodes.rationale: Lessons from building Sonner (13M+ weekly downloads): frictionless DX, good defaults over options, memorable naming, invisible edge-case handling, transitions over keyframes, and a great docs site.

nodes.label: The Gate (four-question filter)
nodes.rationale: Premised on Emil Kowalski's 'You Don't Need Animations': an opportunity finder that suggests motion everywhere is worse than useless, so every candidate must survive frequency, purpose, speed, and function questions before being reported.

nodes.label: Plan Template Structure
nodes.rationale: The executor may be a less capable model with zero context and zero taste, so the plan must contain everything exactly — no references to 'the audit above' or 'the easing we discussed.'

nodes.label: Feel Check
nodes.rationale: Motion can be mechanically correct and still feel wrong, so verification must include an eye-checkable slow-motion/frame-by-frame pass, not just mechanical commands.

nodes.label: Improve-Animations Workflow
nodes.rationale: Recon -> parallel audit -> vet/prioritize/confirm -> write plans mirrors an audit-then-plan workflow so the capable model handles judgment and any cheaper agent handles execution.

nodes.label: Proto-picker Component
nodes.rationale: The picker's appearance is deliberately not a design decision — a fixed dark glass pill that stays identical across every project so it always reads as harness chrome, never part of the design being judged.

nodes.label: Highlight Slide Animation
nodes.rationale: The active pill slides between buttons (250ms strong ease-out) as spatial feedback on the picker itself, while the variant preview swap stays instant since flipping is a 100+/session action under the frequency rule.

nodes.label: Variant Divergence Principle
nodes.rationale: Three tints of the same idea waste the picker — the user learns nothing by flipping between them — so each variant must diverge on a named axis and be defensible shipped on its own.

nodes.label: Remedial Preference Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Fixes are preferred in order: delete the animation, reduce it, fix easing, fix origin/physicality, make interruptible, move to GPU, asymmetric timing, polish, accessibility & cohesion — cheapest and highest-leverage moves first.
